name: Arabic
about: Written right to left. Letters join and change shape; short vowels are usually not written.

phrases.how: Right to left, and letters join: each has a separate, start, middle and end form.
phrases.why: Greet someone in their own script on a card or a note.
phrases.dictation: Five letters, right to left: م ر ح ب ا. Then write them joined.

phrases.how: Dots tell letters apart: ش has three dots, added after the main stroke.
phrases.why: Write a real thank-you card to a host or to family.
phrases.dictation: Four letters: ش ك ر ا. ش has three dots on top.

phrases.how: ء (hamza) marks a short catch in the throat; the long 'ā' is written with ا.
phrases.why: Spot it on a menu, a sign or a bottle label.
phrases.dictation: Three letters: م ا ء. Hamza sits on the line, on its own.

phrases.how: Some letters (ا د ذ ر ز و) never join the next one, so words can have gaps: صد يق.
phrases.why: Sign a note to a friend. Writing it by hand helps you remember it.
phrases.dictation: Four letters: ص د ي ق. There's a gap after د.

phrases.how: و and ا don't connect forward, so واحد is written in pieces: و, ا, then حد.
phrases.why: Read quantities and order one of something off a menu.
phrases.dictation: Four letters: و ا ح د. Only ح and د join.
